name: Lead Exposure Elimination Project (Founders Pledge)
summary: Advocacy for laws against lead in paint in low- and middle-income countries. Founders Pledge's page states a cost per child's lead exposure prevented, $1.66; our bridge turns a prevented exposure into lower blood lead, IQ and earnings with GiveWell's figures.

sections.title: Founders Pledge's figure
sections.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figures, as its recommendation page states them. It publishes no spreadsheet for this recommendation, so these are the model's only evaluator rows.

sections.title: From a child protected to units of value
sections.explainer: charityevals' bridge, not Founders Pledge's: the page doesn't say what a prevented exposure is worth. We assume it lowers a child's blood lead throughout childhood by about 1.5 micrograms per decilitre (our judgment), and value each microgram with GiveWell's lead figures from its Pure Earth analysis: IQ points lost per microgram, earnings per IQ point, shared with the household, plus its allowance for lead's other health effects.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Cost to prevent one child's lead exposure (in expectation)

source.title: Founders Pledge, Lead Exposure Elimination Project (recommendation page)
source.quote: We estimate that it costs $1.66 to prevent one child’s lead exposure (in expectation).

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's figure, quoted on its page (August 2023): "it costs $1.66 to prevent one child's lead exposure (in expectation)". The expectation already allows for the chance that a country doesn't regulate or enforce. Founders Pledge publishes no sheet behind it.

rows.label: Fall in a protected child's blood lead, throughout childhood (µg/dL)
rows.explainer: Our judgment; the page doesn't say. Reference points: children in low- and middle-income countries average about 4.6 µg/dL (Ericson et al. 2021, Lancet Planetary Health); Ambitious Impact's LEEP model attributes 25% of exposure to paint (about 1.2 µg/dL); GiveWell expects 0.8 to 1.0 µg/dL across a covered population in its Pure Earth analysis. Founders Pledge's unit is a child whose exposure is prevented, a more exposed group than the average child, which argues for the upper part of those figures: 1.5, from 0.5 to 4.

rows.label: IQ points lost per µg/dL of blood lead throughout childhood
rows.explainer: GiveWell's figure: 0.2 IQ points per µg/dL from the literature, of which GiveWell keeps 75%.

rows.label: Yearly earnings gain per IQ point
rows.explainer: GiveWell's figure: each IQ point raises yearly earnings by 0.67%.

rows.label: Years from infancy to the start of the earnings gain
Present value of ln(income) per IQ point, per person
rows.explainer: GiveWell's present value (its F62, 0.0763 at its 4%), rebuilt so it moves with the shared discount rate (Your values): the yearly gain, delayed 15 years, paid at the start of each of 40 years.

rows.label: Multiplier for sharing within the household
rows.explainer: GiveWell counts the gain twice because it is shared with the household.

rows.label: GiveWell: adjustment for lead's health effects beyond IQ
rows.explainer: GiveWell's +20% for lead's other harms (heart disease, other morbidity and mortality), as in its own Pure Earth model, so the same change counts the same across models.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: The income gain valued like every income gain on the site (GiveWell's units of value per unit of ln(consumption)), plus GiveWell's 20% for lead's other health effects.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers, advisers and advocates could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: Units of value per dollar, in GiveWell's units (one unit = a year of doubled income for one person). With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
